key_insight: ReToken shows that a single learned token can act as a retrieval query to pick only the most relevant visual tokens from a large cached context. This improves vision-language performance on long visual inputs while avoiding the cost of processing everything at once.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of scaling vision-language models to long visual contexts with many distractors, where accuracy drops and GPU memory makes full-context processing impractical.
method: Train one learnable embedding as an explicit retrieval target.
Use the token to select a sparse set of query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache.
Train on a small image-QA dataset and apply the method to image and video retrieval settings.
impact: For practitioners, ReToken offers a simple and efficient way to handle long visual contexts without major architectural changes. It can improve retrieval quality and reduce memory/computation costs for multimodal systems.

paper_title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
